utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-75-T, the Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President and Your Honours. Douglas Stringer with Matthew Olmsted, Matthew Gillett, and Case Manager Thomas Laugel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Good morning Mr. President, Your Honours. It's Christopher Gosnell co-counsel for Mr. Hadzic and our legal assistant Ms. Liane Aronchick.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. At about 9.30, Judge Mindua will leave court, and we will sit pursuant to Rule 15 bis for the rest of the session. We have one session this morning, and I'll -- I have to keep that tight, because we have other -- other things to do. We have deliberation meetings after that. So please try to end the examination-in-chief within that time and keep some in reserve for your redirect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can we go into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Your witness, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Did you provide testimony before this Tribunal in the case against Slobodan Milosevic on the 29th, 30th, and 31st of January, 2003?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And prior to testifying here today, did you have an opportunity to listen to that prior testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I will now ask you a series of questions to clarify and expand upon your prior testimony. First of all, you testified previously at transcript page 15128 that a unit with Chetnik insignias participated in the 2 May 1991 armed clashes in Borovo Selo. I want to show you 65 ter 149. This is tab 2. And I'm interested in the article on the left-hand side. And this is an article from the 9 May 1991 edition of the "Politika" newspaper entitled "Chetniks Armed with 'Thompson' Rifles." The article reports that 14 Chetniks participated in the armed clashes in Borovo Selo on the 2nd of May. Is that consistent with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is. Perhaps not necessarily in terms of numbers, because I saw some seven or eight Chetniks at the most, whereas I see 14 are mentioned, but the significant -- the difference is not that significant. In any case, this does reflect the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And from what you observed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, the -- I didn't object to the question, but the guidelines on the presentation of evidence prescribe that a witness is first supposed to be asked questions regarding an incident and only once the witness is unable to recall a detail may their memory be refreshed. Those are in the guidelines. So I would suggest we proceed in that manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Olmsted. Sorry. Yes, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'm not showing this document to the witness to refresh his recollection. He testifies about this incident in his prior testimony, and this is to expand upon that and also to corroborate his prior evidence. I will not spend the time going through what he's already testified about because that will be admitted through Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It is a 92 ter witness, Mr. Gosnell. You may proceed, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: From what you could observe that day on the 2nd of May, 1991, what kind of weapons did the Chetniks have in their possession that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As one can read here, I don't find this to be a leading question or the assertion that counsel simply asserted his views, but it is true that the Chetniks did sport Thompson rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, may this be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit Number P239. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: In 1991, did you meet a Serb politician by the name of Milan Paroski?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did. It was in early May in Borovo Selo during a rally.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And did Mr. Paroski speak at that rally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did. He took part in the rally and addressed the gathering. Mainly political matters were discussed in terms of what was going on and what is to be expected and how things would develop.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I'd like to play a video-clip for you. This is 65 ter 4904.1. This is tab 31. And if we could -- we have it paused at the beginning, sir. Can you confirm that the speaker -- I know we see the name there, but can you confirm that the speaker is the person who spoke at that rally in May in Borovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can. He is the second person to the left with the long coat, beige in colour. It's the only kind of coat that -- of that colour in the still.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: Could the microphone be put closer to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: The interpreters have asked if the microphone could be moved up toward the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could play this video now and stop at 1 minute and 14 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And I notice it is subtitled.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] I would like to point out that you now hate me, Croats who live in your houses and were brought here by Pavelic who colonised them here because they were good in slaughtering Serbs. The Hungarians here don't wish to be the same as those in Backa because they primarily serve Tudjman. This is Serbian land and they must realise that they are the intruders and it will be highway for them if it isn't our way. They are perpetually trying to put us down to destroy our borders and our graveyards. Hungarians fear to dig up medieval archaeological finds because all they will find are Serbs. This is the truth. Whoever tells you that this is his land is a usurper, and you have the right to kill him like a dog."

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sir, how does what Mr. Paroski said during -- well, first of all, let me ask you: Do you know where this particular rally took place, this one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in Jagodnjak in Baranja. That's what it was written about so as not to have a leading question again. This was in Borovo Selo and he used literally the same words to put forth his views and introduce himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And that was my next question. What he says during this particular rally is consistent with what he said during the Borovo Selo rally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, may this video-clip be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Is the transcript attached in e-court, Mr. Olmsted?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, we didn't think it was necessary just because it's subtitled, but if you would like us to submit a transcript with it, we can certainly arrange to have that done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's the normal procedure, Mr. Olmsted, so could you please do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: We will take care of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. So then we'll MFI it for the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 4904.1 shall be assigned Exhibit P240, marked for identification until the transcript is provided. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sir, I now would like to show you another video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, can the record reflect that Judge Mindua leaves court and we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis. Thanks. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I'd like to show you another video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could start 65 ter 4895.1. This is tab 17. This one we do have a transcript for, and I want us to play until five seconds into it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Vice President of the presidency of Yugoslavia Branko Kostic visited today Borovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, that was pretty quick, but can you identify the man who is more or less in the centre who is wearing the white suit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can. It's Branko Kostic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, do you recognise the occasion of this footage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know it was sometime in May or June perhaps. I can't say exactly. At any rate, I was there when he visited. I think it was towards the end of May or perhaps June.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And can you tell us where did he visit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He toured everything that was possible to tour at such an occasion since Borovo Selo was there alone. It was not connected with any other populated areas or Dalj. Everything that could be toured, he did tour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And this footage that we see here, is this Borovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is outside the local commune of Borovo Selo. It's the plateau outside the local commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I would now like to play to nine seconds and pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: We'll have to go a little bit further back. I apologise. Okay. Let's play a little bit forward now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Pause.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Kostic --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sir, in your prior testimony at transcript page 15306, you state that the village of Celija was attacked sometime in June or July 1991. Can you tell us who participated in that attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The village of Celija, let's be realistic, was never tactically related or connected to anything in the region. That village has only 30 or 40 houses inhabited by Croats, and they had been a source of problems to the locals of Bobota for going back 50, 60 years. They were never on good terms. I'm only telling you what I heard. The local commune itself organised a blitz operation that lasted only 10, 15 minutes. The residents left the village, and the attackers retreated. Whether somebody was killed in this action, I don't know. I never learned the details of that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Well, do you know whether the local police in Bobota participated in that operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard later, and I'll be quite realistic, that a number of policemen were also involved in the attack on Celija. Not the entire police, but a few of them. And I never verified that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sir, during your prior testimony at transcript page 15173, you mentioned that initially the SBWS TO manned check-points around the region. From August 1991, who began manning the check-points along the borders of the SBWS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Members of the then police, which was stilled called milicija, although there were -- well, I have to say this: The border area which was on the borders of Croatia, although that part of Croatia was still Krajina, there were members of the JNA. However, the check-points inside the area itself were manned by members of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, you testified previously at transcript page 15162 that after the takeover of Dalj, widespread looting took place in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 5589.1 on the screen. This is tab 32. And if we could go to page 10 first.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sir, who is this individual?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know him but only by nickname. Since we are in open session, perhaps I shouldn't tell of his identity right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. Then perhaps we should move to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sir, how did Mr. Stanisic respond when you said that Mr. Hadzic wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He didn't quite like the fact that Goran Hadzic was not there, and at the same time, or so I think, a few seconds later he started shouting at those present in terms of why hadn't Vukovar fallen yet. Find Goran Hadzic. I can't be very specific because it's -- it was a long time ago, and I remember some things while I don't remember other things, but in any case, he wanted everyone assembled in a matter of -- of a couple of hours to have a meeting. Then he went back to his car and headed in the direction of the centre. That was all that Mr. Stanisic said.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And you testified previously that the meeting did take place later that day at the Dalj TO building. Can you tell us, during this meeting what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time of the meeting I was providing security for the building where the meeting was to take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have just one more thing for this witness. It's showing him a video, but I think it's going to -- I can't do it in two minutes or three minutes, so with your leave would it be possible for me to show him the video first thing tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: How long would it take, Mr. Olmsted?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Five -- I think it's under ten minutes certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That won't be a problem. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Very good. Great.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sir, during your prior testimony, and this is at transcript page 15164, you recalled how Milan Martic came to the SBWS region in 1991. Could you tell us approximately when did he come to the SBWS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was sometime in the second half of June or around the middle of June of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: You stated June. Are you sure about that month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so. I think I am. Perhaps the difference is one, two, or five days, but it was definitely in June.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: But it was -- it was prior to the Dalj takeover in August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just note for the record that this is a correction from his prior testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: What were your duties with regard to Mr. Martic's visit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, duties. They weren't duties per se because it was all unofficial, but I gave myself that duty to pick him up and bring him to Borovo Selo. The rest was not in my hands. Whatever time I spent with him was on my personal initiative. I did spend some time with him, but that was it. Nothing special.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: When he arrived, did Mr. Martic tell you where he was coming from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We talked from different sides of the Danube as he was parking his car. He said he was coming from the Presidency and he had been to see Mr. Slobodan Milosevic, who was then the president of Yugoslavia. And he was going to visit us. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I want as though you a video-clip. This is 65 ter 4869.1, tab 15. And if we could start at 10 seconds and pause at 17 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Fully in control of the situation. Martic's Knindzas conquered the base in Osijek and crushed Tudjman's --"

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sir, who are the individuals in this image at 17 seconds?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is an open session? If you really want me to say it, I'll say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Unless, sir, you are worried about your -- what you might say may link you to your former position, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it's not for my sake. I was thinking of you. As far as I'm concerned, I can say it. This is Mr. Goran Hadzic, who was president at the time. And whether this man was a minister or just a commander of the Borovo Selo defence, I don't know. That's Ilija Kojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And can you tell us, where is this meeting taking place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think these are offices of the local commune Borovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could just play to 52 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Reporter: Concerning the situation in this area from Croatian TV that Martic brought tanks, we discussed this with Ilija Kojic, commander of the Territorial Defence, and Mr. Martic, the secretary of the MUP of Krajina. "Ilija Kojic: Well, the current situation is difficult because they're not observing the truce. This was evident last night when over 50 mortar and cannon shells landed in Borovo Selo. They continued targeting Bijelo Brdo throughout the night and this morning. Fighting has been going on since this morning at Palaca and --"

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And Mr. Kojic mentions that over 50 mortar and cannon shells landed in Borovo Selo the night before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll be completely realistic. In the whole time the war lasted, that number of shells did not fall on Borovo Selo. It was five or six shells maximum for perhaps ten days and ten nights. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: May we go into private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Hold on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sir, with the clarifications that you made today, are you satisfied that the testimony you provided in the Milosevic case is accurate and correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am. Definitely. If there are any inconsistencies, that's not deliberate. There can only be mistakes in dates where the exact time is -- where the exact time is required. Everything I say will be truthful and accurate, but please do not hold me to specific dates. There are many documents with records of all my statements. You can compare them all and you can see that they are generally the same. I have nothing else to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And I have to ask one final question: Would you give the same answers today that you gave during your prior testimony if you were asked them again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably. Why not? Of course I would say the same. Perhaps not in the same sequence but it would be the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time we seek to tender this witness's 92 ter statement, which is 65 ter 5790, 5791, and 5792, along with the associated exhibits to that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 5790 shall be assigned Exhibit P245. 65 ter document 5791 shall be assigned Exhibit P246. And 65 ter document 5792 shall be assigned Exhibit P247. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. So the associated documents will be given a number by the registrar and a memo will be circulated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. These are under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, that completes my direct examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Witness, we have only one session available this morning for the direct examination by the Prosecution, and we will your testimony with the cross-examination by the Defence tomorrow morning at 9.00. That means that you are not released as a witness, you are still under oath, and you are not allowed to discuss your testimony with anyone, and you are not allowed to talk to any of the parties as long as you are testifying. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You will be escorted out of the -- yes. Let's go to closed session, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of November, 2012, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.47 a.m.,
